title: Nvidia announced $750bn of AI deals. Its own credit market flinched.
excerpt: Nvidia is working on a fresh round of AI infrastructure deals potentially worth more than $750 billion, Bloomberg reported, accelerating a pattern of investment that critics say inflates demand and valuations across the sector. The response from the debt market was unusually direct. Nvidia’s five-year credit default swap spread surged to a record 82 basis […]
content_html:
Nvidia is working on a fresh round of AI infrastructure deals potentially worth more than $750 billion, Bloomberg reported, accelerating a pattern of investment that critics say inflates demand and valuations across the sector. The response from the debt market was unusually direct.

Nvidia’s five-year credit default swap spread surged to a record 82 basis points on Monday, its largest single-day intraday increase since the contract began actively trading in November 2025, according to ICE Data Services figures cited by Bloomberg. Credit default swaps are effectively insurance against a bond issuer failing to pay.

What is in the $750bn

An AI initiative with SK Group, parent of chipmaker SK Hynix, was unveiled late Friday and is worth more than $500 billion by Nvidia’s own accounting. The two will build more than two gigawatts of AI data centres on the Korean Peninsula, roughly the power required for 1.5 million homes.

Separately, Nvidia is in talks to guarantee as much as $250 billion so OpenAI can lease a 10-gigawatt data centre campus that a SoftBank subsidiary is developing in southern Ohio. It is also discussing financing a further $350 billion of OpenAI chip purchases.

Nvidia also said late Friday it will invest $1 billion in Naver Corp to help fund an AI data centre under construction in South Korea, developed jointly with Brookfield. The funding will let Naver more than triple the size of the facility, and its shares rose more than 8% in Seoul.

The Sutskever deal

On Monday Nvidia announced a long-term partnership with Safe Superintelligence, the lab founded by OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever, reportedly worth $5 billion. Nvidia said the arrangement gave it “rare access into the company’s closely guarded research.”

The deal gives SSI access to Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform and will increase its compute by an order of magnitude. For a company with no product and two years of near-total silence, the validation is arguably worth as much as the silicon.

Why the market reacted

The concern is structural rather than moral. Nvidia takes equity stakes in or guarantees debt for customers such as OpenAI and CoreWeave, which then spend the money on Nvidia hardware, a loop that can make demand look stronger than underlying end-user appetite.

“While Nvidia’s investments and partnerships reinforce confidence in long-term AI buildouts, investors remain concerned about circular financing,” said Gary Tan, a portfolio manager at Allspring Global Investments. “Capital is increasingly being used to fund future AI customers and infrastructure deployments.”

Billy Leung, an investment strategist at Global X Management, framed the OpenAI guarantee as a warning sign rather than a bullish one. “It’s as much a reminder of funding strain in the AI buildout as it is a demand signal,” he said.

Both the IMF and the Bank for International Settlements have flagged AI circular financing as a systemic downside risk.

Huang’s rebuttal

Jensen Huang has consistently rejected the framing, arguing Nvidia’s stakes are small relative to what its partners raise elsewhere. “It’s a small percentage of the amount of money that they ultimately have to go raise,” he said of the CoreWeave investment in January, adding that “the idea that it is circular is, it’s ridiculous.”

On the Korean deals he was expansive. “This is the golden ages for Korea,” Huang told Bloomberg Television, noting the $500 billion figure covers Nvidia’s memory chip purchases as well as SK Group buying Nvidia supercomputers.

That last point matters. The SK arrangement flows in both directions, since Nvidia needs high-bandwidth memory that Hynix and Samsung dominate, which makes it a supply deal as much as a demand one.

Not just Nvidia

Vendor guarantees have spread across the industry. Google agreed to backstop lease payments at five data centre sites for Anthropic, helping the OpenAI rival obtain what amounts to a $35 billion loan.

Nvidia has extended credit further down the stack too. It has offered AI startups compute now and payment later, a structure that solves a customer’s cash problem while booking the revenue.

Much of the resulting obligation sits outside standard debt disclosure. Big Tech’s off-balance-sheet AI commitments have been estimated at around $1.65 trillion, which is why guarantees rather than headline borrowing have become the metric to watch.

The tally so far

Nvidia has announced more than $540 billion of such deals in 2026 alone, excluding the potential OpenAI arrangement. It holds stakes in OpenAI, Marvell, IREN, CoreWeave, and Nebius.

Monday cost it. Nvidia shares fell close to 5% to $196.51, stripping roughly $250 billion from its market value and handing the title of world’s most valuable company back to Apple.

The OpenAI negotiations are early stage and could collapse or change terms, and neither Nvidia nor OpenAI commented. What is already settled is that the credit market has decided this pattern carries a price, and it has started charging for it.

据彭博社报道，英伟达正在开展新一轮人工智能基础设施交易，价值可能超过 7500 亿美元，这加速了一种投资模式，批评者称这种投资模式夸大了整个行业的需求和估值。 债务市场的反应异常直接。

彭博社援引 ICE 数据服务数据显示，英伟达五年期信用违约掉期利差周一飙升至创纪录的 82 个基点，这是该合约自 2025 年 11 月开始活跃交易以来的最大单日盘中涨幅。 信用违约掉期是针对债券发行人未能付款的有效保险。

7500亿美元里有什么

芯片制造商 SK 海力士的母公司 SK 集团的一项人工智能计划于周五晚间公布，根据 Nvidia 自己的核算，该计划的价值超过 5000 亿美元。 两家公司将在朝鲜半岛建设超过 2 吉瓦的人工智能数据中心，大约相当于 150 万户家庭所需的电力。

另外，Nvidia 正在洽谈提供高达 2500 亿美元的担保，以便 OpenAI 能够租赁软银子公司正在俄亥俄州南部开发的 10 吉瓦数据中心园区。 它还正在讨论为购买 OpenAI 芯片再融资 3500 亿美元。

Nvidia 周五晚间还表示，将向 Naver Corp 投资 10 亿美元，以资助与 Brookfield 联合开发的韩国正在建设的人工智能数据中心。 这笔资金将使 Naver 的设施规模扩大三倍以上，其在首尔的股价上涨超过 8%。

苏茨克韦尔交易

周一，Nvidia 宣布与 Safe Superintelligence 建立长期合作伙伴关系，该实验室由 OpenAI 联合创始人 Ilya Sutskever 创立，据报道价值 50 亿美元。 英伟达表示，这一安排使其“难得接触到该公司严密保护的研究”。

该交易使 SSI 能够访问 Nvidia 的 Vera Rubin 平台，并将其计算能力提高一个数量级。 对于一家没有产品并且两年几乎完全沉默的公司来说，验证可以说与芯片一样有价值。

市场为何反应

这种担忧是结构性的，而不是道德性的。 Nvidia 为 OpenAI 和 CoreWeave 等客户提供股权或担保债务，然后这些客户将资金花在 Nvidia 硬件上，这种循环可以使需求看起来比潜在的最终用户胃口更强劲。

Allspring Global Investments 的投资组合经理 Gary Tan 表示：“虽然 Nvidia 的投资和合作伙伴关系增强了人们对长期人工智能建设的信心，但投资者仍然对循环融资感到担忧。” “资本越来越多地用于资助未来的人工智能客户和基础设施部署。”

Global X Management 的投资策略师 Billy Leung 将 OpenAI 的担保视为一个警告信号，而不是一个看涨信号。 他说：“这既是一个需求信号，也是对人工智能建设资金紧张的提醒。”

国际货币基金组织和国际清算银行都将人工智能循环融资标记为系统性下行风险。

黄的反驳

黄仁勋一直否认这种框架，认为英伟达的股份相对于其合作伙伴在其他地方筹集的股份来说很小。 “这只是他们最终必须筹集的资金的一小部分，”他在一月份谈到 CoreWeave 的投资时说道，并补充道，“认为它是循环的想法是荒谬的。”

在韩国交易上，他的态度很豪爽。 黄告诉彭博电视台：“这是韩国的黄金时代。”他指出，5000 亿美元的数字涵盖了 Nvidia 的存储芯片采购以及 SK 集团购买的 Nvidia 超级计算机。

最后一点很重要。 SK安排是双向的，因为英伟达需要海力士和三星主导的高带宽内存，这使得它既是一项供应交易，也是一项需求交易。

不仅仅是英伟达

供应商担保已遍布整个行业。 谷歌同意支持 Anthropic 五个数据中心站点的租赁付款，帮助 OpenAI 竞争对手获得相当于 350 亿美元的贷款。

英伟达也进一步扩大了信用额度。 它为人工智能初创公司提供了“先计算，后付款”的结构，可以在预订收入的同时解决客户的现金问题。

由此产生的大部分义务不属于标准债务披露范围。 大型科技公司的表外人工智能承诺估计约为 1.65 万亿美元，这就是为什么担保而不是整体借款成为值得关注的指标。

到目前为止的统计

仅 2026 年，Nvidia 就宣布了超过 5400 亿美元的此类交易，其中不包括潜在的 OpenAI 安排。 它持有 OpenAI、Marvell、IREN、CoreWeave 和 Nebius 的股份。

周一付出了代价。 英伟达股价下跌近 5%，至 196.51 美元，市值蒸发约 2500 亿美元，并将全球最有价值公司的头衔重新拱手让给了苹果。

OpenAI 的谈判还处于早期阶段，可能会破裂或改变条款，Nvidia 和 OpenAI 都没有发表评论。 已经确定的是，信贷市场已经决定这种模式是有代价的，并且已经开始收费。
